artifacts.summary: Six-phase acceptance-gate remediation plan: live re-measurement ledger, module-count and README figure corrections, s4witness verdict re-recording with attribution, full CI gate re-run, and the PASS WITH FIX TASKS verdict document with fix-task roadmap handoff.

memory_candidates.content: Acceptance-gate verdict grammar for terminal programme gates: emit exactly one of PASS / PASS WITH FIX TASKS / CONDITIONAL / FAIL, and partition criteria into BLOCKING (correctness: capstone and instance axiom-purity via #print axioms, sorry census, axiom census, build/test/import/lint-style exit codes, ratchet exact-set matches) versus NON-BLOCKING (documentation-figure reproduction, pre-existing repo-wide lint debt, out-of-tree probe reproduction). The decision rule that makes this work: a finding is fix-task-needed rather than blocking only when all three of (1) no proof is weaker, (2) the defect is pre-existing or purely documentational, and (3) the fix is independently schedulable. Critically, an UNEXPLAINED regression-corpus divergence is a FAIL even when every build is green -- behaviour preservation is unproven -- whereas a divergence whose cause is identified and chronologically attributed (via git merge-base --is-ancestor showing the causing commit predates the programme) is merely a stale recorded verdict to be re-recorded additively, never deleted. This keeps a gate from either rubber-stamping green builds or blocking on pre-existing debt.
